content: 1. Polatuzumab vedotin undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a substrate of the hepatic enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration of polatuzumab vedotin with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the area under the curve (AUC) of unconjugated MMAE, potentially leading to increased toxicities associated with polatuzumab vedotin. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of pitolisant by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. For patients already taking pitolisant, the pitolisant dose should be reduced by half when initiating strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 3. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Ponatinib increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are required. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Posaconazole also increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Lopinavir decreases the effects of pramlintide through other mechanisms (refer to comments). Ritonavir similarly decreases the effects of pramlintide. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Comment: Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been associated with protease inhibitors. 7. Ritonavir increases the toxicity of pravastatin through other mechanisms (refer to comments). Caution and monitoring are advised. Comment: OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase the risk of myopathy. 8. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of praziquantel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of prednisolone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Prednisone decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel, micronized progesterone, and natural progesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of propranolol by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Quercetin decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quetiapine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both quetiapine and ritonavir can increase each other's toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT intervals or in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT intervals. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of quinidine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Lopinavir and quinine both increase the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 16. Quinupristin/dalfopristin increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. When co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the quizartinib dose to 4 mg/day. Interrupt quizartinib during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors and resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 18. Ranolazine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 19. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of repaglinide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 21. Ritonavir increases rifabutin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ritonavir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Lopinavir similarly increases rifaximin levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase rilpivirine levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of lopinavir and ritonavir via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Avoid co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of Torsade de Pointes. 25. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Lopinavir increases rivaroxaban levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of rivaroxaban with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors due to the risk of significant increases in rivaroxaban levels and bleeding risk. 27. Lopinavir and ritonavir decrease the levels or effects of roflumilast by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Concomitant therapy may reduce therapeutic effectiveness. 28. Ritonavir and lopinavir increase the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 29. Rolapitant increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rolapitant may increase plasma concentrations of CYP2D6 substrates for at least 28 days following administration. 30. Lopinavir decreases the effects of rosiglitazone through other mechanisms (refer to comments). Ritonavir similarly decreases rosiglitazone effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Comment: Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been associated with protease inhibitors. 31. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Ritonavir increases rosuvastatin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 34. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of sacubitril/valsartan by decreasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. 36. Lopinavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Reduce saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Ritonavir increases saxagliptin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. Reduce saxagliptin dose to 5 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Lopinavir and ritonavir increase seladelpar levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Use caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 39. Selpercatinib increases lopinavir toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Ritonavir increases sertraline levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended due to the increased risk of serotonin syndrome. 41. Lopinavir increases sertraline levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity. 42. Ritonavir increases silodosin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Ritonavir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Lopinavir and ritonavir decrease sitagliptin effects through other mechanisms (refer to comments). Caution and monitoring are recommended. Comment: Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance have been associated with protease inhibitors. 45. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases lopinavir toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 46. Ritonavir increases solifenacin levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases lopinavir toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Consider pre-dose and post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at increased risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 48. Sorafenib and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Ritonavir increases sorafenib levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. St. John’s Wort decreases ritonavir levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Stiripentol affects hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol may require dosage adjustments.
